indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: This refers either to the availability of at least one room more than the minimum, or to at least 15% more space than the minimum,
as prescribed by local regulations.

metric.question: Does the housing unit satisfy minimum space requirements associated with the composition of the household that was adopted in the design? (single selection allowed)

options.1: The housing unit does not provide the minimum necessary space.
options.2: The housing unit provides the minimum necessary space.
options.3: The housing unit provides space above the recommended minimum.

indicators.name: Maintaining the quality of spaces and services
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: Strategy is affected by scale according to Section 5.6.3.

metric.question: Is a strategy in place for maintaining the quality of project spaces and services in the medium to long term? (single selection allowed)

options.1: A strategy is not included for the long-term maintenance of project spaces and services.
options.2: A strategy for the long-term maintenance of project spaces and services exists but it is limited to some aspects only (e.g. management of common spaces), with or without a budget.
options.3: A strategy for the long-term maintenance of project spaces and services is fully integrated into the project but no budget is allocated.
options.4: An overall strategy that includes a plan and an appropriate budget is allocated for the long-term maintenance of project spaces and services.

indicators.name: Rental scheme
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

context.question: How is the rental sector characterised at the urban level? (single selection allowed)

options.b: Moderate share of subsidised and social rental (>15% and < 25%).
options.c: Large share of subsidised and social rental (≥25%).

metric.question: What is the rental scheme that is adopted by the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Private rental at market price.
options.2: Private rental at an affordable price (agreed rents).
options.3: Private rental with rent allowances.
options.4: Social rental.

indicators.name: Homeownership scheme
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

context.question: How is the housing sector characterised at the urban level in relation to homeownership? (single selection allowed)

options.b: Mix of private market and subsidised homeownership (both < 60%).

metric.question: What is the homeownership scheme adopted by the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Individual market homeownership.
options.2: Collective homeownership.
options.3: Individual subsidised homeownership.

indicators.name: Pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities
indicators.rule_summary: Average walking time to essential services and amenities, in four bands: 0, 50, 70, 100 (Table 167)
notes: Pedestrian accessibility evaluated according to Section 5.6.6.

metric.question: What is the level of pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities is more than 15 minutes.
options.2: Pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities is between 11 and 15 minutes.
options.3: Pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities is between 6 and 10 minutes.
options.4: Pedestrian accessibility to essential services and amenities is less than 5 minutes.

indicators.name: Accessibility to services and amenities by public transport
indicators.rule_summary: Average public transport travel time to services and amenities, in four bands: 0, 50, 70, 100 (Table 169)
notes: Accessibility by public transport evaluated according to Section 5.6.7.

metric.question: What is the level of accessibility by public transport to services and amenities? (single selection allowed)

options.1: The average travel time by public transport is ≥ 30 minutes.
options.2: The average travel time by public transport is ≥ 22.5 and < 30 minutes.
options.3: The average travel time by public transport is ≥ 15 and < 22.5 minutes.
options.4: The average travel time by public transport is < 15 minutes.

indicators.name: Pedestrian accessibility to public transport
indicators.rule_summary: Average walking distance to the nearest public transport stop, in four bands: 0, 50, 70, 100 (Table 170)
notes: Pedestrian accessibility to public transport evaluated according to Section 5.6.8.

metric.question: What is the level of pedestrian accessibility to public transport? (single selection allowed)

options.1: The average distance to public transport stops is more than 800 m.
options.2: The average distance to public transport stops is between 500 and 800 m.
options.3: The average distance to transport stops is between 300 and 500 m.
options.4: The average distance to transport stops is less than 300 m.

indicators.name: Rental contracts
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: The extent to which a project can promote affordability through rental regulation depends on the existing rental market (including
social rental).

context.question: How would you describe the local rental market in terms of regulatory capacity? (single selection allowed)

options.a: Strongly regulated (the rental sector controls the market through rent caps and rent stabilisation measures).
options.b: Fairly regulated (the rental sector includes some regulations to control rent prices with limited scope).
options.c: Liberalised (the rental sector is entirely controlled by the market).

metric.question: What types of rental contracts are available by the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Only fixed term and short-term rental contracts are offered.
options.2: Only fixed-term rental contracts are offered.
options.3: A mix of fixed-term and unlimited duration contracts are offered. Fixed-term rental contracts are the majority.
options.4: A mix of fixed-term and unlimited duration contracts are offered. Unlimited duration rental contracts are the majority.
options.5: Only unlimited duration rental contracts are offered.

indicators.name: Rents setting
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: The extent to which a project can promote affordability through rental regulation depends on the existing rental market (including
social rental).
Dashes correspond to options that cannot be selected by the user, given the contextual variance.

context.question: How would you describe the local rental market in terms of regulatory capacity? (single selection allowed)

options.a: Strongly regulated (the rental sector controls the market through rent caps and rent stabilisation measures).
options.b: Fairly regulated (the rental sector includes some regulations to control rent prices with limited scope).
options.c: Liberalised (the rental sector is entirely controlled by the market).

metric.question: How are rents set by the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Rents are set above the market price in the neighbourhood.
options.2: Rents are set according to market price in the neighbourhood.
options.3: Rents are set partly at market price and partly according to local rent or ad hoc control regulations that compensate for limited/non-existing regulations.
options.4: Rents are set according to local rent control regulations.
options.5: Rents are set according to ad hoc rent control mechanisms.

indicators.name: Housing typology mix
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

context.question: Does the neighbourhood provide a variation of housing typologies? (single selection allowed)

options.a: Limited mix (clear dominance of one typology).
options.b: Some mix (significant presence of at least two typologies, one of which is multifamily housing).
options.c: Substantial mix (significant presence of three or more housing typologies).

metric.question: How does the project affect the housing typology mix of the neighbourhood? (single selection allowed)

options.1: It decreases the typology mix.
options.2: It maintains the typology mix.
options.3: It increases the typology mix.

indicators.name: Prevention of segregation at the micro-scale
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: A neighbourhood is defined as wealthy/gentrified according to Section 5.8.3.

metric.question: If [the neighbourhood is wealthy or gentrified]1, does the project adopt any form of prevention against segregation at the micro-scale? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Preventive measures are not adopted.
options.2: The project is included within a neighbourhood strategy for social mix, which includes service provision, and measures are implemented at the neighbourhood level to prevent segregation, exclusion, or displacement.
options.3: The project includes services for the new residents and/or in its design attention is paid to not discriminate among residents.

indicators.name: Prevention of gentrification and displacement
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: A neighbourhood is defined as low to -middle-income or gentrifying according to Section 5.8.4.

context.question: If [the neighbourhood is low to middle-income or gentrifying]1, which of the following trends is identified within the scale of the project (i.e. neighbourhood)? (single selection allowed)

options.a: Steep increase (≥ 10%) of housing costs (rents and prices) in the neighbourhood in the last three years.
options.b: Average increase (≥ 3% and < 10%) of housing costs (rents and prices) in the neighbourhood in the last three years.
options.c: Stable or minimal variation (< 3%) of housing costs (rents and prices).

metric.question: If [the neighbourhood is low to middle-income or gentrifying], does the project adopt any form of prevention against gentrification and displacement? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Preventive measures are not adopted.
options.2: Some measures are taken at the project level, but a local comprehensive strategy is not adopted.
options.3: The project is included within a neighbourhood or municipal housing policy for the protection of residents from price increases and displacement, or the project provides ad hoc measures.

indicators.name: Outreach activities for project-related social and cultural services
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Are diverse outreach activities planned to spread the knowledge of and secure recruitment for existing or project-related social and cultural services? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Activities are not planned.
options.2: Yes, to some extent: an outreach strategy exists, but covers only some of the services offered.
options.3: Yes, an overall strategy is in place: a comprehensive outreach strategy exists, covering all services offered, identifying specialised target groups, methodology and communication plans for each service.

indicators.name: Active accessibility needs in the project strategy
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Are active accessibility needs included in the project strategy? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Active accessibility needs for offered services are not taken into account.
options.2: The project partially addresses the issue of accessibility through a preliminary plan.
options.3: The project includes an accessibility strategy based on the analysis of local needs.

indicators.name: Mapping of assets and resources
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Are assets and resources mapped? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Mapping of assets and resources is not integrated or planned.
options.2: A partial preliminary mapping is included in the project without the involvement of the local community.
options.3: A complete mapping of assets and resources is integrated through the involvement of the local community.

indicators.name: Diversification of activities in response to local needs
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Are the activities of the project adequately diversified according to local needs? (single selection allowed)

options.1: The activities of the project are planned (or will be) according to assumptions about local needs without the use of local data.
options.2: The activities of the project are planned (or will be) according to a mapping based on the project team’s knowledge and/or some aggregated data.
options.3: The activities of the project are planned (or will be) according to a mapping based on the collection of disaggregated data and/or the involvement of the local community.

indicators.name: Acknowledgement of cultural and social barriers to accessibility
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: For building and neighbourhood-scale projects, the percentage of vulnerable groups in the neighbourhood context should be compared
with the percentage in the urban context. For urban-scale projects, the percentage in the urban context should be compared with the
percentage in the regional context.

context.question: What is the level of existing vulnerabilities and precariousness (presence of homeless, undocumented migrants, people with mental health problems and/or addictions, unemployed people, etc.)? (single selection allowed)

options.a: The percentage of vulnerable groups is above the average percentage in a broader context.
options.b: The percentage of vulnerable groups is equal to the average percentage in a broader context.
options.c: The percentage of vulnerable groups is below the average percentage in a broader context.

metric.question: To what extent are cultural and social barriers to accessibility acknowledged by the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Cultural and social barriers to accessibility are not identified.
options.2: Cultural and social barriers to accessibility are identified by the project team through a desk review and based on assumed vulnerable groups in the area.
options.3: Cultural and social barriers to accessibility are identified by using various methods (desk review, interviews, surveys, etc.) and based on identified vulnerable groups in the area.
options.4: Cultural and social barriers to accessibility are identified through a co-production process involving relevant stakeholders to promote an intersectional analysis.

indicators.name: Local support networks and trained social workers
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: For building and neighbourhood-scale projects, the percentage of vulnerable groups in the neighbourhood context should be compared
with the percentage in the urban context. For urban-scale projects, the percentage in the urban context should be compared with the
percentage in the regional context.

context.question: Considering the level of existing vulnerabilities and precariousness (presence of homeless, undocumented migrants, people with mental health problems and/or addictions, unemployed people, etc.), what is the need for support networks? (single selection allowed)

options.a: Very high need for support networks: when the percentage of vulnerable groups is much above the average percentage in a broader context.
options.b: High need for support networks: when the percentage of vulnerable groups is above the average percentage in a broader context.
options.c: Moderate/low need for support networks: when the percentage of vulnerable groups is equal to or below the average percentage in a broader context.

metric.question: Does the project involve local support networks or trained social workers? (single selection allowed)

options.1: The project does not employ trained social workers and does not involve any existing local support networks.
options.2: The project acknowledges the importance of relying on qualified assistance through the employment of trained workers, or the use of a local support network, or both.

indicators.name: Needs of vulnerable and marginalised groups covered by activities
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: For building and neighbourhood-scale projects, the percentage of vulnerable groups in the neighbourhood context should be compared
with the percentage in the urban context. For urban-scale projects, the percentage in the urban context should be compared with the
percentage in the regional context.

context.question: What is the level of existing vulnerabilities and precariousness (presence of homeless, undocumented migrants, people with mental health problems and/or addictions, unemployed people, etc.)? (single selection allowed)

options.a: The percentage of vulnerable groups is above the average percentage in a broader context.
options.b: The percentage of vulnerable groups is equal to the average percentage in a broader context.
options.c: The percentage of vulnerable groups is below the average percentage in a broader context.

metric.question: Are the needs of vulnerable and marginalised groups targeted and covered by planned activities? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Needs of vulnerable groups are not specifically targeted and activities are open to all.
options.2: Needs of vulnerable groups are in part covered by the project activities.
options.3: Needs of vulnerable groups are in part covered by the project activities and for the remainder by other targeted local services.
options.4: Needs of vulnerable groups are totally covered by the project activities.

indicators.name: Anti-discriminatory action
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: Dashes correspond to options that cannot be selected by the user, given the contextual variance.

context.question: To your knowledge, can the neighbourhood be described as conflictual? (single selection allowed)

options.a: If [Renovation project] has been selected – Yes: e.g. discriminatory episodes on regular basis; tensions among neighbours or residents that affect daily life; specific social groups excluded by public or common spaces; social groups with no mixing in public spaces or public spaces like schools, community centres, public services).
options.b: If [Renovation project] has been selected – Yes, to some extent: there is respect towards diversity, and positive relationships are being developed, even though discriminatory episodes may occasionally occur in different places, e.g. public spaces, schools, community centres, public services).
options.c: If [Renovation project] has been selected – No: people are usually respectful towards diversity, and groups from different backgrounds and circumstances intermingle and build strong and positive relationships in different places.
options.d: If [Newbuild project] has been selected, check the metric below.

metric.question: Does the project plan anti-discriminatory action? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Such action is not planned.
options.2: Such action is not necessary at the project scale because it is sufficiently developed at a higher level by public authorities, and the users are knowledgeable about it.
options.3: Such action is not necessary at the project level, but it is planned as an important issue.
options.4: Such action is necessary, and it is implemented at the project level.
options.5: Such action is planned (irrespective of context).

indicators.name: Monitoring plan of safety and non-discrimination conditions
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Does the project include a monitoring plan of safety and non-discrimination conditions of the places where activities are carried out? (single selection allowed)

options.1: A monitoring plan is not included.
options.2: A monitoring plan is not elaborated but some measures are planned.
options.3: Yes, a monitoring plan is included.

indicators.name: Involvement of local stakeholders in project meetings
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Considering the following three profiles (i–iii) of local civil society stakeholders, i. Independent citizens, citizen initiatives, neighbourhood boards or associations. ii. NGOs, trade unions, other civil society organisations. iii. Local professionals (e.g. research community, policy experts or officials, independent experts from the economic sector). how would you qualify their involvement in the project participatory meetings? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Active and regular involvement of profile ii or iii of stakeholders, and occasional (or no) involvement of the other two.
options.2: Active and regular involvement of profiles ii and iii, and occasional (or no) involvement of profile i.
options.3: Active and regular involvement of profile i, and occasional (or no) involvement of profiles ii and iii of stakeholders.
options.4: Active and regular involvement of two out of the three profiles of stakeholders (including profile i), and occasional (or no) involvement of the third.
options.5: Active and regular involvement of the three profiles of stakeholders.

indicators.name: Involvement of public and private sector stakeholders in project meetings
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Considering the following three profiles (i–iii) of stakeholders: i. Private entities (corporate). ii. Public entities. iii. Public-private partnerships. how would you describe their involvement in the project participatory meetings? (single selection allowed)

options.1: An occasional (or no) involvement of all stakeholders (public, corporate and public-private partnerships).
options.2: An active and regular involvement of corporate entities and an occasional (or no) involvement of public entities and/or public- private partnerships.
options.3: An active and regular involvement of public and/or public-private partnerships and an occasional (or no) involvement of corporate entities.
options.4: An active and regular involvement of all stakeholders (public, corporate and public-private partnerships).

indicators.name: Contribution of local civil society stakeholders to project design
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Considering the following three profiles (i–iii) of local civil society stakeholders, i. Independent citizens, citizen initiatives, neighbourhood boards or associations. ii. NGOs, trade unions, other civil society organisations. iii. Local professionals (e.g. research community, policy experts or officials, independent experts from the economic sector). how would you describe their contribution to the design of the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: No significant contribution from any stakeholder.
options.2: Significant contribution of profile ii or profile iii of stakeholders and minor (or no) contribution of the remaining two.
options.3: Significant contribution of profiles ii and iii, and minor (or no) contribution of profile i.
options.4: Significant contribution of profile i, and minor (or no) contribution of the remaining two profiles of stakeholders.
options.5: Significant contribution of two out of the three profiles of stakeholders (including i) and minor (or no) contribution of the third profile.
options.6: Significant contribution of the three profiles of stakeholders.

indicators.name: Contribution of public and private sector stakeholders to project design
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: Considering the following three profiles (i–iii) of stakeholders: i. Private entities (corporate). ii. Public entities. iii. Public-private partnerships. how would you describe their contribution to the design of the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: No significant contribution from any profile of stakeholder.
options.2: Significant contribution of profile i or profile ii of stakeholders, and minor (or no) contribution of the remaining two.
options.3: Significant contribution of profiles i and iii, and minor (or no) contribution of profile ii.
options.4: Significant contribution of profile ii, and minor (or no) contribution of profiles i and iii.
options.5: Significant contribution of profiles i and ii, and minor (or no) contribution of profile iii.
options.6: Significant contribution of all three profiles of stakeholders.

indicators.name: Diversity and representativeness of the stakeholders in project design
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: Neighbourhood context should be considered for building and neighbourhood-scale projects, and urban context for urban-scale
projects.

context.question: To your knowledge, how you would characterise the project context in terms of significant presence of social stakeholder groups? (single selection allowed)

options.a: The context is characterised by the dominant presence of one or two stakeholder group.
options.b: The context is characterised by the presence of multiple stakeholder groups.

metric.question: How would you describe the diversity and representativeness of the stakeholder social groups involved in the design of the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Focused on one social group of stakeholders whose presence dominates the design phase.
options.2: Mainly focused on a few social groups of stakeholders.
options.3: Quite diverse and representative (most local social groups are present, only a few are missing).
options.4: Very diverse and representative (all local social groups are present even if in different proportions).

indicators.name: Contribution of stakeholders from vulnerable groups to project design
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix
notes: Levels of contribution defined in Section 5.12.7.

metric.question: How would you describe the contribution of stakeholders related to vulnerable groups to the design of the project? (single selection allowed)

options.1: No contribution.
options.2: Rather insignificant contribution.
options.3: Fair contribution.
options.4: Significant contribution.

indicators.name: Project budget allocated to engagement events
indicators.rule_summary: Fixed questionnaire: one answer, often read against a context question; score from the JRC matrix

metric.question: What is the level of the project budget allocated to engagement events during the design stage? (single selection allowed)

options.1: Very low level of allocated funding (< 3%).
options.2: Low level of allocated funding (3–5%).
options.3: Average level of allocated funding (6–8%).
options.4: High level of allocated funding (9–10%).
options.5: Very high level of allocated funding (> 10%).
